title: Design and validation of canary- and rollback-aware scoring metrics to predict operational risk of agentic NetOps actions
research_question: Can a composite scoring metric (combining verifier coverage, canary deployment simulation success, rollback-success probability, and abstention utility) predict simulated operational risk (outage probability) better than single-factor metrics?
confirmatory_hypotheses: A composite canary-rollback score will have a larger AUC-ROC for predicting simulated runtime outage than any single submetric (e.g., verifier pass rate) on a held-out test set.

Applying a decision threshold on the composite score yields higher practical true-negative rate (reduction in risky full-deployment changes accepted) at comparable true-positive rate than thresholding on verifier pass/fail alone when used with canary deployments.
exploratory_questions: Which submetrics (verifier coverage, canary-sim pass rate, rollback success, LLM-confidence, abstention utility) contribute most to predictive performance in ablation?
How stable are learned composite weights across task clusters (topology/vendor variants)?
How sensitive are operational decision curves to threshold choice and class-imbalance?
benchmark_scope: Synthetic NetOps Task Bank v1 (publicly releasable) consisting of intent-to-configuration tasks, canonicalized vendor-CLI variants generated for open-source network stacks (FRR, Open vSwitch) and containerized network functions.
Sandboxed emulation traces from containerized topology emulators (no proprietary vendor images).
model_scope: Single hosted LLM API (commercial or research-hosted model accessible via API) used only for configuration generation/text-to-config transforms; token-level or sampling-based uncertainty estimated via repeat-sampling where API permits.
No model fine-tuning; no local GPU inference.
transformation_scope: Textual intent -> structured canonical configuration (JSON/YANG-like intermediate) via LLM generation.
Canonical -> vendor-CLI renderer for open-source stacks (deterministic templates).
Deterministic parser from vendor-CLI back to canonical form for equivalence checks.
primary_estimand: Difference in AUC-ROC (composite score vs best single submetric) for predicting binary simulated outage on held-out test tasks.
secondary_estimands: Difference in AUPRC between composite and best submetric.
True-negative rate (TNR) at operationally relevant true-positive rate (TPR) threshold.
Calibration (Brier score) of composite score on test set.
sampling_plan: Construct a reproducible synthetic task bank of 600 unique tasks (intent + topology + vendor-variant). Random RNG seed fixed in preregistration. Split deterministically by hash into: train N=300, validation N=100 (used for cross-validation and hyperparameter selection), test N=200 (held-out, only used once for final evaluation). Task clusters: 10 topology/vendor clusters; tasks distributed evenly (60 tasks/cluster => 30 train,10 val,20 test per cluster). All splits and seeds are recorded and published.
analysis_plan: Compute submetrics per task deterministically (verifier-coverage fraction; canary-simulation pass/fail rate aggregated over deterministic emulator seeds; rollback-success probability estimated via scripted fault-injection trials in the emulator). Train penalized logistic regression (L2) mapping submetrics to binary outage label on train+val via 5-fold cross-validation over the training+validation set (300+100=400). Final weights fixed from cross-validation. Evaluate primary estimand on test N=200: report AUC-ROC, AUPRC, Brier score with 95% bootstrap CIs (10k bootstrap samples capped by wall-clock/compute budget). Compare AUCs using DeLong’s test; primary comparison is composite vs best single submetric. Pre-register primary comparison only; other comparisons are exploratory with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR control reported.
multiplicity_plan: Primary hypothesis: single pre-registered comparison (composite vs best single submetric) at alpha=0.05. Secondary and exploratory outcomes corrected via FDR (Benjamini–Hochberg) where multiple tests apply. Report unadjusted p-values and adjusted FDR q-values; clearly label exploratory analyses.
missingness_plan: Technical failures (emulator crash, verifier timeout) are treated as technical missingness. Automatic retry policy: up to 2 automatic re-executions with identical deterministic seeds. If still failing, mark item as failed-technical, exclude from confirmatory primary analysis, and include in sensitivity analysis: (a) worst-case imputation (assume outage), (b) best-case imputation (assume no outage). All exclusions and counts are logged and published.

risk_factors: Train/test contamination via duplicate or near-duplicate tasks (intent, topology, vendor-variant).
Seed leakage when generating canonical->vendor variants.
Data-derivation drift if template generators reuse identical renderings across splits.
detection_procedures: Deterministic content hashing (intent + topology canonical form + vendor-variant) to detect duplicates across splits.
Approximate nearest-neighbor (token-based Jaccard/MinHash) deduplication to flag near-duplicates.
Seed/hashing provenance checks to ensure deterministic split assignment.
item_flagging_rules: Exact duplicates across splits: automatic exclusion from training (if a test duplicate exists) and relocation to a quarantined replication set for sensitivity analysis.
Near-duplicates (Jaccard similarity > 0.85): flag for sensitivity analysis (no manual adjudication).
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Primary analysis excludes exact duplicates and retains only canonical split-assigned items. Sensitivity analyses evaluate (a) inclusion of near-duplicates, (b) removal of entire flagged clusters. All treatments and counts reported.
residual_uncertainty: Residual semantic similarity not captured by token similarity metrics may remain; placed in remaining_noncritical_uncertainties.

budget_scenarios.description: Conservative feasible run aligned with capability manifest and candidate estimate. One LLM generation call per task (train+val+test = 600 tasks) => 600 model calls. Deterministic verifiers and emulators run on CPU/docker; no human annotation.
transformations: Intent -> canonical JSON via LLM (1 generation call per task)
Canonical -> vendor-CLI via deterministic renderer (no model calls)
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Total tasks = discovery (train+val) 400 + confirmatory (test) 200 = 600 tasks. Planned_model_calls = 1 generation call/task * 600 tasks = 600 calls. This matches the candidate estimated_model_calls (600) and is within the manifest maximum planned_model_calls (10000). Verifiers and emulators execute deterministically in Docker on CPU; no unavailable resources required.

budget_scenarios.description: Larger-budget ensemble sampling scenario to improve calibration and uncertainty estimation: 3 generation variants per task (ensemble/prompt-variants) for richer uncertainty signals.
models: hosted LLM API (3-prompt ensemble per task)
transformations: Intent -> 3 generated candidate canonical configs per task; canonicalization and deterministic renderer applied; ensemble-derived submetrics aggregated
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: 3 generation calls/task * 600 tasks = 1800 model calls. Uses hosted API (allowed) and deterministic downstream processing; increases compute/time cost but remains within the manifest max (10000). Recommended only if budget/time permit and if additional sampling is needed for uncertainty estimation.

power_plan.primary_estimand: Difference in AUC-ROC (composite - best single submetric) on held-out test set (N=200).
power_plan.target_effect: Detect a delta_AUC ≈ 0.07 (composite improves AUC by 0.07 over best submetric), two-sided alpha=0.05, desired power ≈ 0.8.
power_plan.clustering_unit: Task cluster (topology/vendor variant); tasks assumed approximately independent across clusters; intra-cluster dependence assessed in sensitivity analyses.
power_plan.calculation_method: Empirical bootstrap on held-out test set (200) for CI estimation of AUC; DeLong’s test for AUC difference. No analytic AUC-power closed form used; justification: bootstrap CI width with 200 samples expected to detect ~0.07 AUC difference with ~80% probability under assumed baseline AUC 0.75 (assumption below).
assumptions: Baseline best-submetric AUC ≈ 0.75 (conservative estimate from prior small-scale studies in evidence).
Test set size fixed at N=200; tasks approximately IID conditional on cluster stratification.
Bootstrap with 10k resamples (or as many as permitted by wall-clock) provides stable CI; DeLong test assumptions approximately hold for AUC comparison.
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With Ntest=200 and baseline AUC=0.75, a delta_AUC ≈ 0.07 is approximately detectable with bootstrap CIs and DeLong’s test at ~80% power; if baseline AUC is higher (e.g., 0.80) detectable delta increases. Report observed effect sizes with CIs rather than relying solely on p-values.
sensitivity_analyses: Bootstrap-based power sensitivity varying test N in {100,200,300} to show effect-size detection limits.
Per-cluster stratified evaluation to assess intra-cluster dependence impact.
High-powered scenario (3-sample ensemble) re-evaluated to measure calibration improvements.

transformation_families: Canonical -> vendor-CLI deterministic rendering (template-driven for FRR/OVS)
semantic_equivalence_checks: Roundtrip equivalence: canonical -> vendor-CLI -> parser -> canonical' and deterministic equality or specified semantic-preserving equivalence (reachability matrix equality) using emulated topology.
Reachability matrix comparison between generated configuration and canonical specification using deterministic emulation for a subset.
automatic_rejection_rules: If parser fails to parse vendor-CLI output deterministically -> automatic exclusion of that generated item with logged reason.

If roundtrip canonical' differs syntactically from canonical beyond pre-registered tolerance thresholds (e.g., >2 differing statements) -> automatic flag and exclusion from training; included in diagnostic counts.
If verifier input generation produces syntax errors or verifier timeouts -> automatic retry (up to 2) then mark as technical failure.
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Automated deep-audit on a random 5% sample of transformations using full emulation-based semantic equivalence checks (reachability and ACL-equivalence); audit is automated (no human adjudication).
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Unit-test suite of deterministic parsers and renderers using a curated set of 100 canonical examples with known vendor renderings; these unit-tests run in CI and are published.
residual_risks: Template-driven renderers for open-source stacks may not capture proprietary vendor semantics; residual semantic drift remains and is reported as noncritical uncertainty.
Roundtrip equality tolerances may hide subtle semantic differences not exercised in emulation sample; flagged as residual risk.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: External-validity: composite weights learned on synthetic/open-source stacks may not generalize to proprietary vendor devices or production traffic distributions.
Canary simulation fidelity: containerized emulators of FRR/OVS may not capture all production device failure modes or vendor-specific behaviors.
Threshold-transferability: operational thresholds may require per-organization tuning; decision-curve results are illustrative rather than universally prescriptive.
Hosted LLM API nondeterminism: model-side nondeterminism and token-prob availability vary by provider; uncertainty estimation may be imperfect.
